video_title: The transformative potential of solid-state transformers
gist: Nphase co-founder Ragu Balure explains how solid state transformers built from ~1,000 modular 5 kW GaN power converters can replace copper-and-iron transformers, with AI data centers moving to 800 V DC (pilots 2027, ramp 2028) and grid batteries as the beachhead, utility-scale solar next, and the 60-million-unit neighborhood distribution transformer fleet as the long-term prize. He argues semiconductor cost curves will reach parity in 3-5 years, while durability (10-year warranty vs 50-year iron) and utility conservatism remain the key hurdles.

themes.theme: Why the transformer is due for disruption

insights.claim: Conventional copper-and-iron line-frequency (60 Hz) transformers have barely changed in a century; they are cheap, reliable and efficient but 'dumb', and the US currently cannot make them fast enough, with multi-year lead times.
insights.speaker: David Roberts
insights.so_what: Transformer shortage is a structural bottleneck for grid buildout; supply-constrained incumbents and any credible substitute both benefit.
insights.quote: Right now, the US can't make them fast enough. It takes years to get one.

insights.claim: Conventional transformers can only do AC-in/AC-out at fixed voltage ratios: they cannot convert AC to DC, cannot handle DC, and are blind to harmonics and noise created by fluctuating loads like data centers.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Defines the functional gap SSTs fill: DC-native loads/sources and power-quality management are the wedge use cases.

insights.claim: Bidirectional power flow from rooftop solar, home batteries and bidirectional EV chargers means the grid must add intelligence (monitoring and control of power flow) at every node rather than rely only on brute-force generation additions.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Supports demand for grid-edge power electronics, VPPs and smart distribution equipment as DER penetration rises.
insights.quote: So it's no longer a unidirectional power flow. Now the power flow has become completely birectional.

insights.claim: Power electronics have taken over phones, cars and nearly everything else but not the grid, mainly because of utility institutional conservatism around reliability combined with the recent arrival of enabling compute and wide-bandgap devices.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Adoption pace is gated by institutions more than physics; watch utility pilots and standards as leading indicators.

insights.claim: Roughly 60 million neighborhood pole-top/pad-mount distribution transformers exist in the US, and the host has read that around half are near the end of their rated life, creating a massive replacement wave.
insights.speaker: David Roberts
insights.so_what: A looming replacement cycle is the largest addressable market for SSTs and a demand tailwind for conventional transformer makers in the interim.

insights.claim: The host warns that the current transformer shortage is prompting a surge of conventional transformer manufacturing, risking a lock-in of decades-lived dumb transformers before SSTs are ready.
insights.speaker: David Roberts
insights.so_what: Near-term orders likely still go to conventional transformers; SST penetration of distribution may be delayed by this installed-base lock-in.

themes.theme: SST technology: semiconductors replace copper and iron

insights.claim: A solid state transformer uses semiconductors (wide-bandgap silicon carbide or gallium nitride) to chop power at high frequency (10 kHz to hundreds of kHz vs 60 Hz), shrinking the magnetic component and enabling any-voltage-to-any-voltage, AC or DC, fully bidirectional conversion with monitoring and control.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Core technology mechanism; wide-bandgap semiconductor suppliers are direct beneficiaries of SST adoption.

insights.claim: Ragu Balure argues semiconductor-and-software-based products keep compounding cost, reliability and performance improvements, whereas copper and iron costs asymptote because materials are bought by weight.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Framework for betting on power-electronics substitutes over materials-intensive incumbents across clean energy hardware.
insights.quote: copper and iron is copper and iron I mean I buy them by weight

insights.claim: The combination of cheap compute and the availability of wide-bandgap devices is what has made solid state transformers viable today, per Ragu Balure.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Wide-bandgap supply-chain maturity is the enabling factor to track for SST commercialization timelines.

insights.claim: Nphase's SST builds a 5 MVA transformer from about 1,000 modular 5 kW power converters, analogous to how data centers scale by adding GPUs tied together (e.g. Nvidia NVLink72), while others use ~100 kW building blocks.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Modular architecture lets SST capacity scale linearly and leverages high-volume electronics manufacturing; a key differentiator versus monolithic SST designs.

insights.claim: Nphase's SST modules contain almost no copper (transformer core weighing hundreds of grams per 5 kW module), with silicone potting the largest weight contributor, shifting supply chains to standard surface-mount PCB manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: SSTs reduce exposure to copper constraints that limit conventional transformer and grid buildout.

insights.claim: Nphase chose gallium nitride over silicon carbide (moving roughly 10 years ago) because GaN-on-silicon allows higher switching frequencies, simpler manufacturing with larger ingots, and bidirectional GaN on a single die versus two dies for silicon carbide.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Most SST competitors use silicon carbide; a GaN-based architecture is a differentiated bet that could shift wide-bandgap demand mix.
insights.quote: Silicon carbide is the second hardest material in the world

insights.claim: Ragu Balure argues that GaN is effectively a commodity and that, because Nphase uses only a thin epitaxial GaN layer on silicon, it has no material exposure to Chinese gallium supply concerns.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Counter to the consensus worry about China gallium controls; investors should verify GaN supply-chain resilience independently.
insights.quote: we are not subject to any GAN supply chain concerns

insights.claim: Nphase's control architecture is single-stage, 250-500 kHz switching with predictive control computed on its own custom ASIC (five ASIC generations, nine inverter generations), plus soft switching that minimizes harmonics and EMI.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Proprietary silicon and control IP form Nphase's moat claim; fast response time also underpins its battery-savings pitch in data centers.

themes.theme: Data centers and 800V DC as the beachhead

insights.claim: AI training loads swing from 10% to 100% about five times per second, and SSTs plus batteries are needed to keep these fluctuations from being reflected back onto utility grids and rotating machines.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Load-smoothing equipment (SSTs, batteries) becomes a required spend for AI data center interconnection.

insights.claim: Rack power densities have climbed from about 30 kW to 150 kW to 250 kW today, with 1 MW racks being discussed; at 50 V a 1 MW rack would need 20,000 amps, making legacy low-voltage DC delivery infeasible.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Rising rack density forces a power-architecture overhaul inside data centers, creating a new equipment market.

insights.claim: Data centers are pushing toward 800 V DC in the white space (borrowed from EV DC fast-charging voltages), which cuts current to servers by roughly 18-20x and dramatically reduces copper and losses; the electrical code limit is 1,500 V DC.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: 800 V DC adoption is the key catalyst for SSTs and DC power equipment suppliers; track hyperscaler announcements and standards.

insights.claim: Ragu Balure expects 800 V DC data center pilots in 2027 and deployments ramping in 2028 (possibly first deployments in late 2027), with quick adoption for any company delivering viable SSTs.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Sets a concrete timeline: SST revenue inflection would be 2028+ for data centers.
insights.quote: 2027 you should expect pilots at 800 volts DC and then deployments in 2028

insights.claim: An SST converting directly from 34,500 V AC medium voltage to 800 V DC can eliminate the transformer, PCS, double-conversion UPS and multiple downstream conversion stages, with estimated efficiency gains of about 4.5-5%.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Threatens incumbent UPS and multi-stage power-chain equipment vendors while improving data center economics.

insights.claim: Because data centers are power-constrained, a ~5% efficiency gain can be redeployed as ~5% more GPUs, raising revenue and tokens per watt rather than just saving energy.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Frames SST value in revenue terms for hyperscalers, supporting willingness to pay a premium.

insights.claim: Nphase pitches that its fast-response SSTs can let data centers rely on a distant 2-4 hour battery energy storage system (e.g. ~4 GWh, 30+ acres, a quarter mile away for a gigawatt campus) instead of per-rack battery backup units, freeing up to ~50% of side-rack space for compute.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: If validated, reduces demand for in-rack BBUs and increases demand for utility-scale co-located BESS.

insights.claim: Hyperscalers are the first SST market because they have money and an urgent need for speed, mirroring how many clean energy technologies use deep-pocketed early adopters to fund early deployment and ride down the cost curve.
insights.speaker: David Roberts
insights.so_what: Data center demand is the funding engine for SST cost reduction; later markets depend on its success.

insights.claim: SSTs placed in front of grid-scale batteries replace the power control system plus medium-voltage transformer with a single device, so Nphase plans to address data center and BESS markets almost simultaneously.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: BESS integrators and PCS/transformer suppliers face a potential single-device substitute.

insights.claim: The US utility-scale PV market is estimated at 30-40 GW for 2027, with global markets larger, representing the next big SST opportunity after data centers and batteries.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Sizes the second SST market; displaces central inverters plus step-up transformers.

insights.claim: Nphase oversizes its SSTs by about 6% (roughly 60 extra 5 kW modules in a 5 MVA unit), which Ragu Balure says could raise PV power-conversion reliability enough to move from typical 5-year warranties toward potentially 20-year warranties, a 3-4x improvement.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Longer warranties could change PV lifetime O&M economics and pressure central inverter incumbents.

insights.claim: Nphase's SST modules weigh about 8 lbs each and are hot-swappable from a backplane, and the company is building (not yet built) a cobot to replace failed modules at medium voltage without human technicians.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Could cut O&M costs and regulatory/training burden for field service if delivered.

themes.theme: Nphase scale, track record and SST economics

insights.claim: Nphase has shipped 30+ GW of power electronics, about 90 million microinverters, and is installed in about 5.2-5.3 million homes, with a historical failure rate around 500 DPPM (0.05%).
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Reliability and scale track record is Nphase's main credential for entering the SST market.

insights.claim: Nphase's SST power modules share about 85% supply chain overlap with its existing solar and battery microinverters, and it already has capacity for 3 million devices per quarter (12 million/year, 50+ GW).
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Existing manufacturing scale lowers capex and ramp risk for Nphase's SST entry, and FEOC compliance positions it for critical-infrastructure procurement.

insights.claim: Ragu Balure frames transformers as critical infrastructure requiring foreign-entity-of-concern (FEOC) compliance, contrasting with Europe's roughly 200 GW of solar that is not necessarily under its own control.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Domestic, FEOC-compliant suppliers may gain an edge as grid power electronics face national-security scrutiny.
insights.quote: You don't want to have what's happening in Europe with 200 gawatt of solar that is not necessarily in their control.

insights.claim: SSTs are more expensive than conventional transformers upfront (host cites 5-10x; Ragu Balure disputes that magnitude), but the case rests on total cost of ownership: replacing multiple devices, higher system efficiency, and a semiconductor cost curve.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Upfront premium means early adoption only where system-level savings are large (data centers, BESS).

insights.claim: Ragu Balure believes SSTs can reach cost parity with conventional analog transformers within roughly 3-5 years, though not within the next two years, contingent on scale, automated manufacturing and an efficient supply chain.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Cost parity would open the 60-million-unit distribution transformer market; a key milestone to track.
insights.quote: I don't know in how many years, you know, it could be 3 years, it could be 5 years.

insights.claim: Nphase targets 98.5% SST efficiency versus about 99% for iron transformers, and Ragu Balure says efficiency is not a limiting factor.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Efficiency gap is small; the system-level gains outweigh the device-level loss.

insights.claim: Nphase's SST currently carries a 10-year warranty versus 50+ year lifespans for iron transformers; Ragu Balure sees 25-year warranties as achievable (as with its rooftop microinverters) but calls 50 years a stretch with current technology.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Durability is the main gap for pole-top replacement; replacement-cycle costs could slow utility adoption.
insights.quote: with current technology 50 is a bit of a stretch

themes.theme: Distribution grid prize, utilities and policy

insights.claim: The long-term prize for SSTs is the neighborhood distribution transformer, which Ragu Balure calls a necessity rather than a nice-to-have given bidirectional distributed energy, but proving reliability comes before cost in that market.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: The largest TAM is the slowest to adopt; reliability proof in data centers and PV is the gating step.

insights.claim: Ragu Balure says Nphase is having more discussions with utilities about SSTs than expected and adoption could be faster than people think, though he knows of no US utility deploying SSTs on pole tops yet.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Watch for first utility distribution pilots as a signal the bigger market is opening.

insights.claim: SSTs interconnecting front-of-meter PV, BESS, data centers and fast DC charging at 34.5 kV or 13.8 kV will give grid operators firsthand experience with SST behavior, building the confidence needed for neighborhood deployment.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Behind-the-meter and front-of-meter installs serve as a de facto pilot program for distribution adoption.

insights.claim: Solid state transformers are intrinsically current-limited, which Ragu Balure sees as an advantage for fault handling: with rate-of-change-of-current detection and emerging solid state breakers, faults can be isolated without dumping 100,000-amp surges.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Complementary demand for solid state circuit breakers; protection-scheme redesign is a hurdle for utilities.

insights.claim: Ragu Balure argues cyber risk from software-controlled grid devices is solvable, citing device birth certificates at manufacture, segregation of safety from application functions, and controlled upgrades, while acknowledging an ongoing race against AI-driven attackers.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Cybersecurity standards and guardrails will shape procurement of networked grid hardware.

insights.claim: Key near-term enablers for SST adoption are updated UL standards, National Electrical Code changes, first-responder training and lawmaker education, with cyber guardrails built in.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Standards-body progress is a trackable leading indicator for SST market timing.

insights.claim: The US grid is roughly 500 GW and needs to grow 2-3x for electrification, and both speakers argue grid modernization with smart power electronics is needed within 5-10 years, with data centers only the leading indicator.
insights.speaker: Ragu Balure
insights.so_what: Multi-decade grid capex supercycle extends well beyond AI; positions grid power electronics as a secular theme.
insights.quote: This needs to happen in the next 5 to 10 years.
